plain.li: [faith:devout] I'll tell it the way it was told to me, when I was small and the nights were long.
[faith:devout] It isn't a list of rules. It's how we try to live, and why.
[faith:devout] Ask whatever you like. I'd rather have a hard question than a polite silence.
[faith:devout] When things were at their worst last season, this is what I held on to.
[faith:devout] There's a story about the first of us to walk this road. It goes like this.
[faith:devout,lowtech] My grandmother said these words over every harvest. I'll say them now.
[faith:devout,!lowtech] Some of it is written down. Most of it you only learn by living it.
[!faith:devout] So that's why you never work at dawn.
[!faith:devout] Mine says something like that too, in other words.
[!faith:devout] Can I ask something without it sounding rude?
[!faith:devout] Say that last part again?
[faith:wavering] I used to be as sure of mine as you are of yours. Go on.

warm.li: [faith:devout] Thank you for coming, all of you. It means more than you'd think.

blunt.li: [!faith:devout] I came for the warm seat. The talk's not bad either.

cheerful.li: [!faith:devout] Is there singing after? There should be singing.

gloomy.li: [faith:devout] The world takes a great deal from us. It doesn't get to take this.

cold.li: [!faith:devout] It hangs together better than I expected.

plain.li: My faith doesn't hold with being preached at. I'll be in my room.
I'll leave {FAITH} to those who hold it.
[faith:devout] We don't sit through other people's sermons. It's nothing against anyone.
They can have their evening. I know what I believe.

gloomy.li: Every faith wants one more believer. Not this one.

cold.li: Two hours of being told what to think. No, thank you.

plain.li: [poor] {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH}, but the words wouldn't come right, and one by one the listeners found reasons to leave.
[poor] The evening of {FAITH} came to very little. {PAWN_nameDef} lost the thread halfway, and the fire was more interesting.
[poor,believers] Only the faithful came to hear {PAWN_nameDef}, and they had heard it all before.
[good] {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH}, plainly and without hurry, and answered every question put to {PAWN_objective}.
[good] An evening of {FAITH}: {PAWN_nameDef} told the old stories, and the listeners stayed to the end.
[good,altar] By the {PLACE}, {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH}, and for once nobody was watching the door.
[good,believers] The faithful of {FAITH} sat together while {PAWN_nameDef} spoke, and went to bed steadier for it.
[good,guide] {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH} as its moral guide, and spoke well.
[fine] {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH}, and the talk went on long after, in twos and threes, about what it means to believe anything.
[fine,!believers] Those who came to hear {PAWN_nameDef} speak for {FAITH} stayed late, even the doubters.
[fine,believers] The faithful of {FAITH} heard {PAWN_nameDef} out to the last word, and sat on together long after.
[fine,altar] At the {PLACE}, {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH} as if to each of them alone. It was very still afterwards.
[fine,moved] {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH}, and those of other faiths who came walked home very thoughtful.
[speaker,poor] Spoke for {FAITH} tonight and made a mess of it. I'll do better next time.
[speaker,good] Spoke for {FAITH} this evening. They listened, and some of them stayed to ask questions.
[speaker,fine] Tonight I spoke for {FAITH} and every word came out right. I'm still too awake to sleep.
[listener,unmoved] Went to hear {OTHER_nameDef} speak for {FAITH}. I see why it matters to {OTHER_objective}. It isn't mine.
[listener,poor] {OTHER_nameDef} tried to speak for {FAITH}. It didn't go well, and I felt for {OTHER_objective}.
[listener,moved] {OTHER_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH} tonight. I keep going over what was said.
[listener,fine,moved] I went to {OTHER_nameDef}'s evening out of curiosity and came back with more questions about my own faith than I took.

blunt.li: [listener,unmoved] {FAITH} evening. Good stew after. That's my review.

plain.li: [faith:devout] Ours after supper, theirs at first light. That's fair.
[faith:devout] We'll leave it tidy for them, the way we'd want it left for us.
[!faith:devout] I didn't know they sang at theirs.
[!faith:devout] Two faiths, one roof. We'll manage.
[!faith:devout] Strange, hearing someone else's words in this place. Not bad. Strange.

blunt.li: [!faith:devout] As long as nobody sits in my seat.

plain.li: The council has named {FAITH} the colony's faith. I'll keep mine all the same, quietly if I have to.
So {FAITH} is the colony's faith now. Nobody asked me, and I won't forget that.
[faith:alone] One faith for the colony, and I'm the only one left holding mine.

gloomy.li: One faith for the colony, and it isn't mine. Some home this is.

cold.li: {FAITH} is the colony's faith by the council's word. Noted.

plain.li: [faith:devout] From today our faith is the colony's. We'll carry it gently.
[faith:devout] Nobody will be made to believe anything. But the door is open.
[!faith:devout] So that's that, then.
[!faith:devout] I'll believe what I believe, decree or no decree.
[!faith:devout] Does this change who does the cooking? No? Then fine.

warm.li: [faith:devout] Whatever you hold to, you're one of us. That hasn't changed.

gloomy.li: [!faith:devout] One faith for everyone. It never ends well in the stories.

plain.li: Before we start: a word from {FAITH}, as the council asked.
Let's begin as {FAITH} teaches, with a moment's quiet.
[faith:devout] A blessing on this meeting, in the way of {FAITH}. Now, to business.
May we choose well tonight. {FAITH} asks no more of us than that.

cheerful.li: A word from {FAITH} first, and I promise it's a short one.

cold.li: The decree asks for a word from {FAITH}. Here it is: be honest in what you say tonight.

plain.li: {NAME}, and {A_nameDef} reminds the council that the evening belongs to {SUBJECT}.
[first] {NAME} comes round for the first time. Those of {SUBJECT} have the chairs out already.
[years] {NAME} again, {YEARS} years on. {SUBJECT} keeps its evening.
[tradition] {NAME}: the evening of {SUBJECT}, as every year, and everyone welcome.

gloomy.li: {NAME}. {A_nameDef} says a hard year is when the colony needs its evenings most.

plain.li: {NAME}: the evening of {SUBJECT}. I sat at the back and listened.
[first] The first {NAME}. We'll see if it lasts.
[tradition] {NAME} again. The same words every year, and I find I like that.
[faith:devout] {NAME}. The faith spoken for, as it should be every year.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about {SUBJECT} on {NAME}.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} what {B_pronoun} believes, on {NAME}.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the story {A_pronoun} likes best from {NAME}.
[way:faith] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} set out chairs for tomorrow's evening of faith.
